vector: One-click SMS links, network injection, zero-click iMessage exploits
objective: Full device surveillance: messages, calls, microphone, camera, location
source: Amnesty International Security Lab, 'Forensic Methodology Report: How to catch NSO Group's Pegasus' (2021); Citizen Lab peer review
os: Fast security patching; exploit mitigations (ASLR, pointer authentication); BlastDoor sandbox for iMessage parsing; iOS Lockdown Mode for high-risk users; regular reboot clears non-persistent implants
store: FINDING: no effective control - delivered by exploits, never through an app store, so pre-publication vetting and store removal do not apply
mdm: Compliance policy enforcing minimum OS/patch level with conditional access; mobile threat defense (MTD) checking indicators of compromise; supervised-device restriction of iMessage/FaceTime for high-risk staff

vector: SMS phishing ('missed parcel') links to sideloaded APK; worm-like re-sending to the victim's contacts
objective: Steal banking credentials via overlays; intercept SMS one-time passwords
source: Europol press release (June 2022); NCC Group / Fox-IT, 'Flubot: the evolution of a notorious Android banking malware' (2022)
os: Per-source 'install unknown apps' permission (Android 8+); Restricted Settings block Accessibility for sideloaded apps (Android 13+); SMS permissions limited to the default SMS app role; on-device Play Protect scan
store: Limited: app was sideloaded, not published. Post-publication style control still applies through Play Protect scanning of sideloaded APKs and Safe Browsing blocking of the download URLs
mdm: Policy blocking unknown sources in the work profile; app allow-listing; MTD phishing-link and Accessibility-abuse detection; conditional access to banking/corporate apps only from compliant devices

vector: Fake Adobe Flash Player update on compromised websites; abuses Accessibility to make itself the default launcher
objective: Change the device PIN and encrypt files, then demand a Bitcoin ransom
os: Android 7+ stops device-admin apps resetting an existing PIN; scoped storage (Android 10/11+) limits which files an app can encrypt; Accessibility consent screens and Restricted Settings; sideload gating
store: Limited: distributed outside the store. Play Protect on-device scanning and Safe Browsing warnings are the only store-side controls
mdm: Enforced cloud backup of corporate data; remote lock/wipe and re-provision; block unknown sources; containerisation keeps work files outside the personal side the malware runs in

timeframe: Tracked by Google from early 2017; analysis published January 2020
vector: Google Play apps that look legitimate, heavy obfuscation and code downloaded at runtime; up to 23 apps submitted in one day
objective: Sign victims up to premium SMS / WAP (carrier) billing services
source: Google Security Blog, 'PHA Family Highlights: Bread (and Friends)' (2020)
os: SEND_SMS is a runtime (dangerous) permission; premium short-code confirmation prompt (Android 4.2+); notification-listener access needs a separate user grant, limiting OTP theft
store: Play SMS/Call Log permission policy (2019) restricting SEND_SMS to default SMS apps; static + dynamic vetting of submissions; about 1,700 Bread apps caught before any download; post-publication removal
mdm: App allow-listing in the work profile; MTD flagging premium-SMS behaviour; FINDING: carrier-billing blocks on corporate SIMs are an operator control, outside MDM reach

vector: About 300 apps on Google Play with hidden bot code
objective: Application-layer HTTP(S) DDoS attacks from at least 70,000 IPs in 100+ countries, sometimes linked to ransom notes
source: Joint report by Akamai, Cloudflare, Flashpoint, Google, Oracle Dyn, RiskIQ and Team Cymru (Cloudflare blog, 28 Aug 2017)
os: Background-execution limits and visible foreground-service notifications (Android 8+); per-app data-usage visibility. FINDING: INTERNET is a normal install-time permission, so the OS cannot stop bot traffic
store: Pre-publication vetting; post-publication removal of ~300 apps and Play Protect removal from already-infected devices
mdm: App allow-listing; per-app VPN / network monitoring for work apps; MTD detecting abnormal traffic; non-compliant devices blocked from corporate resources
